svg.aria-label: A ledger-style timeline of Getty Images from January 2025 to October 2026, one row per event, colour-coded. Red rows are the merger, lawsuits and debt; amber rows are about AI; black rows are the business itself. January 2025: agrees a 3.7 billion dollar merger with Shutterstock. October 2025: borrows 628 million at 10.5 percent to fund it, held in escrow, costing 44 million in interest and fees. November 2025, amber: loses most of its UK copyright case against Stability AI. December 2025, black: best year in its history, 981 million revenue, up 4.5 percent. January 2026: appeals court upholds a 2023 warrant judgment. April 2026: pays two warrant holders 110.9 million, borrowing 120 million to do it. May 2026: UK regulator allows the merger only if Shutterstock sells its editorial arm. June 2026, amber: OpenAI display deal, shares jump as much as 145 percent in a day. July 2026: merger called off after more than 100 million in fees; a court directs a further 67.8 million warrant judgment plus 9 percent interest, about 92 million owed. August 2026, black: second-quarter revenue down 2.5 percent, subscribers down 25 percent, going-concern warning. September 2026: uses the grace period on its 14 percent notes; the NYSE suspends the shares at 12 cents. October 2026: prepackaged Chapter 11, the Getty family and Koch take it private and more than 500 million of debt is cut. Only the two amber rows are about AI.

g.text: EIGHTEEN MONTHS, FROM MERGER TO CHAPTER 11
Red: the merger, the lawsuits and the debt. Amber: AI. Black: the business itself.
Borrows $628m at 10.5% to fund it, held in escrow
Loses most of its UK copyright case against Stability AI
Best year in its history: $981m revenue, up 4.5%
Appeals court upholds a 2023 warrant judgment
Pays two warrant holders, borrowing $120m to do it
UK regulator: only if Shutterstock sells its editorial arm
OpenAI display deal; shares jump as much as 145% in a day
Merger called off after more than $100m in fees
Court directs a further $67.8m warrant judgment, plus 9%
Uses the grace period on its 14% notes; NYSE suspends at 12¢
Prepackaged Chapter 11; Getty family and Koch take it private
Two amber rows are about AI. Getty's own filing says AI pressure alone would not have forced Chapter 11.
